other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 4795, Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act of 2026

summary: The Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act of 2026 is a bill that sets rules for colleges and universities participating in federal student aid programs and Title VI international education programs. It bans these schools from engaging in certain commercial boycotts of Israel unless there is a valid business reason. It also requires schools receiving Title VI funds to certify annually that they allow equal access for students and faculty to participate in academic programs involving Israel.

affected_groups.effect: Must avoid commercial boycotts of Israel not based on valid business reasons and submit annual certifications regarding academic programs to remain eligible for certain federal funds.
Guaranteed equal terms and conditions to participate in academic programs involving Israel and home institutions compared to other foreign countries.

key_provisions: Prohibits institutions of higher education that participate in federal student aid programs from engaging in nonexpressive commercial boycotts against Israel.
Defines a nonexpressive commercial boycott as a commercial action intended to limit commercial relations that is not based on a valid business reason.
Requires colleges and universities receiving or applying for Title VI funds to submit an annual certification by July 31.
Mandates that the annual certification ensure students and faculty can participate in academic programs in Israel under the same terms and conditions as programs in other foreign countries.

Mandates that students and faculty from postsecondary institutions in Israel are allowed to participate in the certifying institution's academic programs under the same terms and conditions as those from other foreign countries.
Establishes a sense of Congress that limiting cooperative efforts with a major strategic partner does not serve the security, stability, and economic vitality of the United States.
